01 / The idea

What problem does it solve?

LLMs can write fluent answers, but they do not automatically know the contents of your private documents. VectorCraft demonstrates the retrieval layer that can supply relevant evidence before generation.

⌕

Search by meaning

Keyword matching looks for words. Semantic search compares embeddings so differently worded text can still be considered related.

▤

Turn documents into evidence

Documents are split into manageable chunks, embedded, stored, and retrieved as candidate context for a question.

✧

Understand RAG end to end

Inspect the question, retrieval results, chunk text, and distance values instead of treating the LLM answer as a black box.

Important distinction: VectorCraft is a learning and experimentation project. A retrieved distance is not an answer-confidence percentage, and retrieval does not guarantee that an LLM response is correct.

03 / System design

Architecture from the project README

This diagram follows the architecture documented in the VectorCraft GitHub repository: Client → Spring Boot REST API, connected to the vector engine, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Ollama.

VectorCraft · architecture from repository

Provided architecture diagram
01

Vector engine

The custom search implementations provide three ways to find nearest vectors: Brute Force, KD-Tree, and HNSW.

02

Persistence

PostgreSQL stores document data, chunks, and vector payloads used by the application.

03

Model and cache integrations

Ollama provides embeddings and generation; Redis is used as an optional answer cache.

04 / Vector index lab

Three ways to find nearby vectors

Choose an algorithm to compare its intuition and trade-offs. The mini visualization below is illustrative, not a benchmark of the running backend.

Exact baseline

Brute Force

Compare the query vector with every stored vector, then rank candidates by the selected distance or similarity metric.

Strength: straightforward and useful as a correctness baseline. Trade-off: work grows with the number of vectors.

Search: O(N·D)Exact ranking
Nearest-neighbour conceptIllustrative 2D projection
Stored vectorsQuerySelected neighbours
Select “Visualize search” to highlight nearby illustrative points.
Algorithm details: Brute Force is the exact comparison baseline. KD-Tree partitions vector space and can help in suitable low-dimensional settings. HNSW builds a navigable graph for approximate nearest-neighbour search. Actual speed and recall depend on data, dimensions, and configuration; measure them rather than assuming one algorithm always wins.
05 / RAG walkthrough

From a question to a grounded answer

Select each stage to see what the system does and what to inspect. This walkthrough describes the project workflow; it does not call a live backend.

SELECTED STAGE

01 · Ask a question

A user submits a question from the browser interface. The API receives the request and starts the RAG workflow.

  • Input: a natural-language question and retrieval options.
  • Inspect: request validation and returned response metadata.
  • Goal: answer a question using relevant stored document evidence.
▤

Chunking

Long documents are split into smaller passages. Chunk size and overlap influence the context available during retrieval.

⌕

Relevance filtering

The system can apply a configurable threshold to avoid sending weakly related retrieved chunks to generation.

◷

Cache

Redis can reuse cached RAG responses for matching requests until the configured TTL expires; document-version-aware keys help avoid stale results.

07 / Key terms

Mini glossary

Short explanations for readers new to AI retrieval.

Embedding

A list of numbers representing aspects of a text's meaning as learned by an embedding model. Similar texts may have vectors that are close under a chosen metric.

Vector database / index

A system that stores or indexes vectors and searches for nearest neighbours. VectorCraft demonstrates custom Java index implementations alongside persisted document data.

Cosine similarity / distance

A measure based on the angle between vectors. Check whether an implementation returns similarity or distance, because their ordering conventions differ.

RAG

Retrieval-Augmented Generation: retrieve relevant information first, then provide that information as context to a language model generating a response.

HNSW

Hierarchical Navigable Small World, a graph-based approximate nearest-neighbour method that trades exactness for efficient search on many workloads.

Hallucination

A generated statement that sounds plausible but is unsupported or incorrect. Retrieval can provide evidence, but it does not eliminate hallucinations.

Chunk size and overlap

Chunk size controls passage length; overlap repeats a small region between adjacent chunks so important context near boundaries is less likely to be lost.

TTL cache

Time-to-live sets how long a cached value can remain eligible for reuse before it expires.

08 / Project maturity

What this project demonstrates — and what comes next

A good case study distinguishes implemented capabilities from future production hardening.

PROJECT CAPABILITIES

Current learning scope

  • Custom Brute Force, KD-Tree, and HNSW search approaches.
  • Document ingestion, chunking, embedding, and semantic retrieval.
  • RAG question-answering flow with retrieved evidence inspection.
  • PostgreSQL persistence, Flyway migrations, and Redis caching.
  • Browser-based learning and experimentation interface.
PRODUCTION HARDENING

Next improvements to consider

  • Add authentication, authorization, and upload limits before public exposure.
  • Add rate limiting, request validation, and secure error handling.
  • Benchmark latency, memory usage, and recall against a reproducible dataset.
  • Add observability, backups, and clear operational health checks.
  • Deploy behind HTTPS with secrets stored outside source control.
Honest performance note: this page does not claim a measured speedup or production scale. Use the benchmark endpoint and repeatable test data to produce evidence before publishing numerical performance claims.
